Topic: Pure Fourier Series: Decoding Signals into Simple Harmonics

Target audience: University students (Engineering/Physics/Mathematics)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisites & Intuition (0:00-0:45)

Lecture lines:
Periodic signals repeat their behavior over time.
Like coordinates, sine waves act as basic building blocks.
A musical chord is a sum of simple tones.

Planned animations:
FadeIn Dot at (-2,0) #FF0000 Label "A"
FadeIn Dot at (2,0) #00FF00 Label "B"
Draw Arrow from A to B color #FFFFFF
Flash Arrow #FFFF00 scale 1.1
FadeOut all objects

Section: section_2 — The Fundamental Hypothesis (0:45-1:45)

Lecture lines:
Any periodic function can become an infinite sum.
We add waves, increasing their frequency each step.
Harmonics layer together to define complex shapes.
Edges sharpen as we add more harmonic terms.
The square wave emerges from these simple layers.

Planned animations:
Write MathTex "H_0: \mu = 0" center #FFFFFF
Flash MathTex #FF0000 scale 1.2
Show Square #0000FF background #222222 around MathTex

Section: section_3 — Calculating Coefficients (1:45-3:15)

Lecture lines:
Fourier coefficients act as volume knobs for harmonics.
Integration extracts the weight of each specific frequency.
Orthogonality ensures different waves do not interfere.
Adjusting coefficients changes the resulting wave shape.
Think of this like a signal mixing board.

Planned animations:
Write MathTex "c_n = \int f(x) e^{-inx} dx" center #FFFFFF
Animate color of "c_n" to #FF00FF
Draw border around integral #00FFFF scale 1.0

Section: section_4 — Visualizing the Series (3:15-4:15)

Lecture lines:
Fourier series can be viewed as rotating gears.
Phasors spin at speeds determined by their frequency.
The path of the final gear traces complex shapes.
Epicycles draw any silhouette with pure harmonic rotations.
Geometry visualizes the math of oscillating signals.

Planned animations:
FadeIn Sine Wave path color #FFFF00
Animate oscillation of wave across screen
Highlight peak at (0,1) with Dot color #FF0000

Section: section_5 — Application & Summary (4:15-5:00)

Lecture lines:
Fourier series compress images into simple frequency lists.
Headphones cancel noise by generating opposite waves.
Complex time-domain signals become ordered frequency lists.

Planned animations:
Write text "Application: Signal Processing" #FFFFFF
Draw icon Square representing a signal #00FF00
Flash signal representation #FFFFFF scale 1.1

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        self.wait(2)
